Definition: , or (shorter) οἶμαι middle voice apparently from G3634; to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion):--suppose, think.
BiblicalUsage: Oiomai means to suppose, to think, to be of the opinion. John supposes in John 21:25 that the world itself could not contain the books if all Jesus did were written, and Paul says in Philippians 1:16 that some preach Christ supposing to add affliction to his bonds. James 1:7 warns the double-minded man: let not that man think he shall receive anything of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe supposing is a thin ground to stand on, and the man who only thinks he will receive has already missed the faith that receives.
